AbstractText.Label: RATIONALE
AbstractText.content: Choledocholithiasis in common bile duct (CBD) stump after Roux-en-Y hepaticojejunostomy (RYHJ) is incredibly rare and its pathophysiology is poorly understood.

AbstractText.Label: PATIENT CONCERNS
AbstractText.content: A 79-year-old woman was admitted to our hospital with upper abdominal pain radiating through to the back in November 2016.

AbstractText.Label: DIAGNOSES
AbstractText.content: Abdominal computed tomography (CT) scan and magnetic resonance cholangiopancreatography (MRCP) revealed filling defects in CBD stump, chronic pancreatitis, and dilatation of CBD stump and main pancreatic duct (MPD).

AbstractText.Label: INTERVENTIONS
AbstractText.content: During the endoscopic retrograde cholangiopancreatography (ERCP), cannulation proceeded easily from MPD to CBD through a variant pancreatic duct, and then white crushed stones extracted from the CBD stump. Elemental analysis and infrared spectrophotometry demonstrated that the main constituent of the calculi was calcium carbonate.

AbstractText.Label: OUTCOMES
AbstractText.content: After a therapeutic ERCP, the patient's symptoms disappeared, and a 9-month follow-up indicated no remaining stones or lithiasis relapse.

AbstractText.Label: LESSONS
AbstractText.content: This type of choledocholithiasis in CBD stump after RYHJ has never been reported before. We nominated it as "pancreatogenic choledocholithiasis," and pancreatobiliary reflux caused by a variant pancreatic duct may be the main cause.

Article.ArticleTitle: Pancreatogenic choledocholithiasis in common bile duct stump after Roux-en-Y hepaticojejunostomy: A case report.
